subject: physical-education
title: Performance task build: racquet or paddle skills
essentialQuestion: How can understanding individual skill development help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

lessonFamilyPlan.instructionalPurpose: build a bounded plan that transfers the target to an accessible setting
lessonFamilyPlan.guidedEmphasis: Stage the access check, setup, safe simulation or description, evidence choice, and finish before combining the plan.
lessonFamilyPlan.independentEvidence: Complete a fresh safe simulation or described plan with honest scope and guardian authority where required.
lessonFamilyPlan.evidencePurpose: planning, decision quality, application, reflection, and completion

goal: I can build a bounded plan that transfers the target to an accessible setting for racquet or paddle skills, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Short path, clear space, controlled finish. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Model ready, contact, and recovery without an object or implement.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: balloon, rolled socks, paper target, or short adult-approved household paddle substitute.
Use an open hand and imaginary object; no racket, net, wall, or sport facility is needed.
movementCues: READY with the full swing or reach path clear.
TRACK the soft or imaginary object into a comfortable contact area.
CONTACT in front or beside the body with a short controlled action.
RECOVER to a stable ready position before the next choice.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Use one short action at a time, say the main cue before the attempt, keep the project lifetime activity choice concrete, and ask a trusted adult to confirm any required permission or space check.

movementModel.title: Model for racquet or paddle skills
movementModel.startingPosition: Begin seated or standing with a stable base, a short empty-hand reach, and a clear arm-and-implement buffer.
movementModel.action: Track, make a short controlled contact motion toward a paper or imaginary target, and recover to ready.
movementModel.keyCue: Short path, clear space, controlled finish.
movementModel.commonError: Taking a large fast swing before checking the complete path.
movementModel.correction: Remove the implement, shorten the path, slow the motion, and freeze at contact and recovery.
movementModel.notice: Notice clear space, contact position, and recovery rather than power.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice clear space, contact position, and recovery rather than power.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Check the complete swing path before each attempt and switch to empty-hand shadow practice whenever clearance is uncertain. No hard object, full-force swing, overhead smash, long implement, or strike toward a person or breakable.

guidedPractice.prompt: Stage the access check, setup, safe simulation or description, evidence choice, and finish before combining the plan. Model ready, contact, and recovery without an object or implement. Apply it to racquet or paddle skills.
guidedPractice.support: Use the model cue: Short path, clear space, controlled finish.
guidedPractice.feedback: If the target is unclear, return to the starting position and use this correction: Remove the implement, shorten the path, slow the motion, and freeze at contact and recovery.

guidedPractice.prompt: Use one short tap or shadow contact toward a large close target.
guidedPractice.support: Watch for this contrast: Taking a large fast swing before checking the complete path.
guidedPractice.feedback: Keep the safe version when the learner can show or explain notice clear space, contact position, and recovery rather than power.

practiceProgression.successCheck: Name what changed and keep the same cue, control, decision, and safety boundary.

practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No hard object, full-force swing, overhead smash, long implement, or strike toward a person or breakable.

independentActivity.title: Fresh application: racquet or paddle skills
directions: Select a fresh safe target and show or describe one controlled ready-to-recovery sequence.
Use this cue or decision: Short path, clear space, controlled finish.
Provide the selected evidence without a recording or body metric.
independentActivity.freshTask: Complete a fresh safe simulation or described plan with honest scope and guardian authority where required. Select a fresh safe target and show or describe one controlled ready-to-recovery sequence.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Trace a short empty-hand contact path.
Freeze at ready, contact, and recovery with continuous breathing.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Clear one full arm-and-implement length on every side. Remove hard objects, people, pets, windows, and breakables from the target direction. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: balloon, rolled socks, paper target, or short adult-approved household paddle substitute.
householdSubstitutes: Use an open hand and imaginary object; no racket, net, wall, or sport facility is needed.
prohibited: No hard object, full-force swing, overhead smash, long implement, or strike toward a person or breakable.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit no-equipment route: shadow the ready/contact/recovery sequence, point to the safe path and target, and explain the control cue.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Check the complete swing path before each attempt and switch to empty-hand shadow practice whenever clearance is uncertain.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.seated: Use a stable seated position and preserve the Short path, clear space, controlled finish. evidence through upper-body movement, pointing, gesture, object modeling, or description.
adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for racquet or paddle skills, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for racquet or paddle skills.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Short path, clear space, controlled finish. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit no-equipment route: shadow the ready/contact/recovery sequence, point to the safe path and target, and explain the control cue.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit no-equipment route: shadow the ready/contact/recovery sequence, point to the safe path and target, and explain the control cue.
adaptationRoutes.describedOrDecisionRoute: Describe, draw, gesture, point, sign, or model Select a fresh safe target and show or describe one controlled ready-to-recovery sequence. This is a complete equal-credit route when movement is not appropriate.

accessibleAdaptation: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice clear space, contact position, and recovery rather than power. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit no-equipment route: shadow the ready/contact/recovery sequence, point to the safe path and target, and explain the control cue.
activitySteps: Choose a standard or equal-credit response route.
Read the STOP AND TELL rule.
Complete the warm-up when it applies.
Use the safe finish when it applies.
Answer the short reflection or leave it blank.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Taking a large fast swing before checking the complete path.

learnerEvidence: One guided response using Short path, clear space, controlled finish..
One fresh bounded application or complete described equivalent for racquet or paddle skills.
One cue, decision, safety, or next-step explanation.
evidenceExpectations.observer: A learner may self-check a cue and a trusted human may review the selected evidence. A Tutor, browser, camera, wearable, or self-report cannot certify physical completion, guardian permission, or safe return.
doNotCollect: weight, appearance, body composition, calories, body shape, fitness norms, speed versus peers, or athletic talent
diagnosis, disability reason, symptom history, or private medical information
photo, video, audio, wearable data, location proof, or exercise log

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for racquet or paddle skills; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Model ready, contact, and recovery without an object or implement.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Short path, clear space, controlled finish.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Taking a large fast swing before checking the complete path. — with this correction — Remove the implement, shorten the path, slow the motion, and freeze at contact and recovery.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Use one short tap or shadow contact toward a large close target.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Select a fresh safe target and show or describe one controlled ready-to-recovery sequence. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice clear space, contact position, and recovery rather than power. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.

may: offer an approved presentation or activity route
coach how the learner presents their own evidence
route to rest, stop, retry, or adult handoff
mustNot: cannot diagnose, prescribe, rehabilitate, or give medical clearance
cannot claim unapproved observation or certify physical completion
cannot override rest, stop, adaptation, guardian authority, professional authority, or safe return
cannot choose the answer or action for fresh independent evidence

Track, make a short controlled contact motion toward a paper or imaginary target, and recover to ready.
Short path, clear space, controlled finish.

privacySafeScenario: Use a supplied or invented non-personal example of racquet or paddle skills; do not disclose private health information or recreate a hazard.
studentTask: Complete a fresh safe simulation or described plan with honest scope and guardian authority where required. Select a fresh safe target and show or describe one controlled ready-to-recovery sequence. Use any approved standard or equal-credit route. Name the cue or decision that controlled the result; no body metric, comparison, recording, or physical-completion claim is required.
knowledgeCheck: State the starting position, action, key cue, common error, and correction for racquet or paddle skills. Then distinguish optional REST / ADJUST from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME.
completionCriteria: The learner uses a safe setup or accurately describes it for racquet or paddle skills.
The learner applies Short path, clear space, controlled finish. in one guided attempt and one fresh application or complete described equivalent.
The learner distinguishes learner-controlled rest from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME conditions.
Any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route earns equal credit for the same cue or decision evidence.
adaptationChoices: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice clear space, contact position, and recovery rather than power. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
extensionChallenge: Apply racquet or paddle skills under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

optionalReflection.prompt: Which cue, decision, safety check, or adaptation preserved the target for racquet or paddle skills, and what would you keep or change in a next safe attempt?

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
